fresh_checks.check: Linear trace compactness and ideal equivalence do not ensure finite extended Monge--Ampere mass.
General-measure equation regimes retain the semipositive model/lower-mass or arbitrary-big BMP/positive-reference-volume hypotheses; minimal ordinary-type Lp existence is different.
Individual exact threshold equality at zero lower mass remains open for general positive-threshold L1 data, despite exponential scalar and measure convergence.
The root space has a complete sum norm; root-only completeness is equivalent to finite upper mass. Root tails and selected-sequence uniform integrability have distinct attainment conclusions.
Smooth strict and semipositive dual attainment give their stated exactness and uniqueness; capacity convergence still needs its genuine smaller-background envelope, which entropy does not supply.
Interior regularity retains global Lp, Holder or boundary-trace hypotheses; local smooth density alone has the stated compact counterexample.
Zero-density nonuniqueness with three positivity components does not refute continuous positive adjoint uniqueness; Lp exponential selection can coexist with nonuniqueness.

Fixed-density positive volume is independent of the smooth positive probability measure, while the infimum over densities may vanish; bigness implies positivity but the arbitrary-nef converse remains open.
Trace normalization preserves the Gauduchon quotients; lambda D<=A proves determinant collapse and shows that noncollapse along one threshold-minimizing sequence implies bigness.

The closed-nef positive-intersection Grauert--Riemenschneider bridge is not refuted by either cited Hopf or lower-mass example. Aeppli density prescription alone does not control determinant-to-trace normalization.
The determinant endpoint exponent and supremum are n/(n-1) and v_minus^(-1/n); subcritical estimates need neither mass property, while balancedness plus BMP is insufficient at the endpoint.
Primitive elliptic-bundle curvature is obtained by a mean-zero Poisson equation. The quotient period, rank-one form, balancedness, sign ddc omega=-c squared and fiber normalization give volume 3TA.

Cube expansion and Stokes give the exact negative vertical Dirichlet mass variation and upper mass 3TA. Nonzero real curvature excludes pluriclosed metrics and closed Kahler currents; zero real class gives c=0. The canonical bundle descends with the stated frame corrections.
The periodic variance argument bounds the range by T and 2M, integrates the cubic deficit and proves sharpness by periodic convolution and strict scaling.

Separated positivity implies p'>-1 and A(1-kappa p squared)>0; fiber integration yields the positive lower bound. Radial amplitude M0 gives the exact positive nonattained infimum, without proving a lower bound for all potentials.

The K3 lattice and period argument excludes curves by adjunction and divisors by projection/Stokes; the external period/Kahler-cone inputs retain their cited scope. The unrestricted primitive lower-mass problem remains open.

The qualitative nef-and-big null-locus theorem is separate from its numerical mass hypotheses and the positive-lower-volume/Guan--Li flow theorem. Determinant degeneration alone does not locate analytic trace concentration.
Once bigness of the flow limit is known, the cited parabolic result gives smooth convergence off the non-Hermitian locus; unrelated big-class incompleteness does not decide the nef flow question.

Scalar potential corrections preserve exterior derivative; balanced trace does not imply ellipticity. The subtraction-cost identity needs a smooth positive segment and retains its differential correction at nonclosed endpoints.
Closed restricted invariants, actual trace types and LCK Lee/twisted-class equations have distinct domains; ordinary Hermitian perturbations do not substitute for those invariants.
Nef degeneration orders can be fractional, unequal or zero and obey one-sided modification comparisons. Metric completion is posed on a specified finite-dimensional unit-volume cone.

Continuous adjoint uniqueness is stronger than smooth and generic uniqueness; moment compactness and scalar reconstruction do not settle it. Measurable weighted products need separately justified multiplication.

Weak ideal-envelope limits may lose mass and ideals. One-sided order, zero/all-obstacle hypotheses and positive-volume cutoff conditions retain their precise scopes; the comparison is not itself a metric.

Curve polar variation gives complete models including zero mass and atomic nearest-ideal retraction. Restricted product/degeneration metrics and two-sided positive-background transport do not cover the full higher-dimensional boundary.

Exact trace realization requires equality on every prime divisor of every smooth modification; a divisorial part on one model or an exceptional cocycle is insufficient. System recovery beyond BMP lacks a replacement uniform deficit estimate.
Kernel lower limits retain closed curvature, intrinsic growth dimension and relative canonical Jacobians. Fiber-selected o(m^q) approximation is not proved for every Hermitian selecting weight.
The growing-jet Gaussian transition retains its exact radius and normalization. The known remainder estimate mR_m^(2r+1)=q_m R_m/r=o(1) settles q_m=o(m^(1/(2r+1))), leaving larger growth open.

Singular-space equations beyond the explicit cone constructions still require finite mass, descent and specified-type uniqueness; conformal Gauduchon existence supplies neither these equations nor a Green operator.
